title: Pool constraint visualizer — proposal and sketch notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch + interaction notes for a compact 'Pool Constraint Visualizer' that helps SREs and capacity owners quickly triage why a dedicated capacity request failed, how reservations/rescheduling would impact latency/cost, and to propose quick fixes (scale-up, reassign reservation, relax constraints). Aim is a single-pane view for incident and planning workflows, complementary to the existing capacity cartography and reservation timeline screens.

Problem statement (observed pain):
- On-call and capacity owners currently jump between the pool timeline, reservation editor, and infra logs to debug allocation failures. Slow triage = customer impact.
- Current UI surfaces raw reservation conflicts but not derived constraint causes (e.g., node-affinity + quantization profile mismatch).
- Need a way to simulate a targeted fix and see immediate effect on headroom/latency/cost.

Primary users and personas:
- SRE on-call (fast triage, minimal clicks, keyboard-friendly)
- Capacity planner / infra PM (what-if planning, bulk edits)
- Solutions Eng / Customer success (explain to customers why reserved capacity is constrained)

Goals and success criteria:
- One-pane summary that surfaces the top 3 constraint causes for a given pool or reservation within 2 clicks.
- Interactive 'what-if' slider to simulate adding N GPUs or relaxing affinity and see a simple delta on request success rate / estimated p95 latency.
- Exportable snapshot (PNG + text summary) for incident notes and customer comms.

High-level components (wireframe elements):
1) Header: Pool selector + time-range quick chips + incident tag (links to oncall incident if present).
2) Constraint heatmap: rows = constraint types (GPU type, quantization, region, tenancy, firmware), columns = resource units (node groups). Color intensity = rejection rate / severity. Hover shows recent sample traces and top failing reservation IDs.
3) Top-3 causes card: auto-extracted root-cause suggestions with single-click actions (open reservation editor, propose temporary quota bump, fallback-to-hosted).
4) What-if bar (compact): slider + action toggles (add GPUs, relax node-affinity, change quantization profile). Live preview shows delta: success %, est p50/p95, monthly delta cost.
5) Conflict timeline (mini): compact strip showing reservation windows and overlapping conflicts; draggable to open full timeline.
6) Quick commands rail: keyboard-accessible commands (scale pool +5, force-reassign reservation, dry-run) with confirmations.
7) Details pane (collapsible): raw allocation logs, relevant tickets, and links to customer-facing commits/PRs.

Interaction notes / microflows:
- Flow A (incident triage): User selects pool -> heatmap auto-highlights constraint with highest recent rejections -> clicks 'Propose fix' -> toggles slider to add 2 GPUs -> immediate preview shows failure rate drops from 18% -> user clicks 'dry-run' -> system runs scheduler simulation and returns 'compatible' -> user triggers a temporary burst request (opens Dedicated API call modal).
- Flow B (capacity planning): User sets time-range to next 30 days -> uses what-if to simulate anticipated reservations -> saves a scenario -> assigns a scenario tag to a rollout ticket.

Wireframe annotations (sketch-level visual cues):
- Heatmap should be keyboard accessible; allow arrow keys to move between constraint rows and enter to open details.
- Color palette: use low-saturation reds and amber to avoid alarm fatigue; primary action color reserved for commit actions.
- Compact mode for on-call: collapse details pane and expand Top-3 causes to fill view.
- Mobile/Tablet: show simplified 'single cause' focus card and a single action button (Propose fix).

Data mapping / backend signals required:
- Sampled scheduler rejection metrics (reason codes aggregated by reservation id and pool).
- Node inventory by GPU type, quantization capability, region, and firmware label.
- Reservation metadata: customer, policy tags, pinned model version, quantization profile.
- Cost model: per-GPU hourly cost + estimated token throughput delta mapping to latency change (simple function).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Which rejection reasons do we surface by default? (Proposal: show only top 8 reason buckets; allow drilling into all).
- How to keep cost estimation conservative and auditable? need input from pricing.
- Scheduling simulation: integrate with existing dry-run API vs build simplified local simulator. Decision pending.
- Access controls: who can propose/apply temporary bursts? map to RBAC roles.

Backlog candidates (priority suggested):
- RED-XXXX: prototype heatmap component + sample dataset (P0)
- RED-XXXX: wire 'what-if' slider to dry-run API (P1)
- RED-XXXX: export snapshot + incident attachment flow (P1)
- RED-XXXX: keyboard nav and compact on-call layout (P2)
- RED-XXXX: cost-model review with finance (P2)

Prototype notes (next steps):
- Designer: Diego to produce 3 fidelity mockups (full, compact, mobile) by 2026-02-05.
- Eng: Marcus to build a lightweight heatmap React component and API contract by 2026-02-12.
- Data: Priya to prepare a 7-day sampled rejection dataset for the prototype.
- Run an internal guerilla usability session with 3 SREs once mid-fidelity exists.

Rough UX sketches (textual):
- Sketch A: Left column = pool selector + quick actions; middle = heatmap (expandable rows); right = top-3 causes + what-if. Footer = conflict timeline.
- Sketch B (compact): Header + single cause card + big action button + small timeline.

Notes to self / quick links and context snippets:
- Slack thread: #infra-pools thread (Jan 9) where customer reported a reservation rejecting due to 'quant-mismatch' — link: slack://channel?team=T123&id=C321
- Related doc: capacity-reservation-playbooks (internal, see Confluence).
- Existing screens to reference: capacity-cartography, reservation-editor, pool-activity-timeline.

Acceptance criteria for initial PRD:
- MVP heatmap renders for selected pool and time-range using sampled data.
- What-if slider calls dry-run API and displays delta numbers.
- Export snapshot button produces PNG + one-page text summary.

Notes on uniqueness vs existing console screens:
- This is NOT a replacement for capacity cartography; instead: single-pane actionable triage view focused on constraint diagnosis + simulation.
- Emphasis on quick hypothesis test (what-if) and exportable incident artifacts.

Appendix: quick glossary used here:
- Constraint heatmap: a condensed matrix that aggregates rejection reasons across node groups and constraint types.
- What-if: short-lived simulation that applies hypothetical changes without mutating live state.
- Dry-run: existing scheduler API that returns allocation decisions without committing.

If this direction looks reasonable I will turn these notes into an annotated mid-fidelity prototype and attach sample datasets for the prototype build.

Unresolved: RBAC specifics and cost-model anchoring. Will loop in finance and security next week.

-- Aisha (notes)
